fixes.explanation: An army camp? Friend, I love the energy, but Moses doesn't say that. He says the LORD will establish the place “…as a dwelling for His Name…” (Deuteronomy 12:5). A dwelling is a home. A home means people arrive, and somebody's glad to see them. I know a little about being glad to see a newcomer, and nobody has ever hugged a barracks.

The foreigner is a good guess, friend, but he's not the name Moses reads out here. After the sons, daughters, menservants and maidservants, Moses says “…the Levite within your gates, since he has no portion or inheritance among you.” (Deuteronomy 12:12). The Levite is the one added to the rejoicing. I think it's a lot like checking the cookie box for the name on the tag, and this tag says Levite.

Baked just right, friend! Moses says, “Both the ceremonially clean and unclean may eat it as they would a gazelle or deer…” (Deuteronomy 12:15). One meat, and two kinds of people welcome at the table. No separate lines, no second table. I've waited at the back of a drawer, so I know how good it feels when nobody gets left out.

You got it, baker! Moses says, “The blood of your other sacrifices must be poured out beside the altar of the LORD your God, but you may eat the meat.” (Deuteronomy 12:27). The burnt offerings go on the altar, meat and blood. For the other sacrifices, the blood gets poured out and the meat is for eating. Two sets of instructions, and you kept them straight. I'd need a sticky note, friend.

That's the one, friend! Moses puts these words in Israel's mouth: “How do these nations serve their gods? I will do likewise.” (Deuteronomy 12:30). The warning is about asking how they serve their gods with the plan to do the same. Then he says it plainly: “You must not worship the LORD your God in this way…” (Deuteronomy 12:31). Israel is to worship the LORD His way, and not borrow anybody else's recipe.
